children: Commodity markets traded mixed on September 23, with oil prices drifting lower as Saudi Arabia began restoring crude supply through a key pipeline to the Red Sea, while gold remained steady as traders monitored the US-Iran talks for cues on energy costs and the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

Oil prices drifted lower on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia began restoring crude supply on a critical pipeline to the Red Sea and on hopes for a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran war through talks at the UN in New York.
Brent crude futures fell 7 cents, or 0.07%, to $99.18 a barrel while West Texas Intermediate futures fell 35 cents, or 0.39%, to $90.17 per barrel.
In precious metals, gold was steady as traders monitored progress in talks between the US and Iran for clues on how
energy costs will influence the Federal Reserve’s path for interest rates.
Bullion was trading around $4,360 an ounce, after swinging between gains and losses on Tuesday before ending the session up 0.4%.
Silver advanced 0.5% to $67.40 an ounce, after gaining 1.6% the day before. Platinum and palladium edged higher.

The dollar steadied near its strongest level in two months on Wednesday on prospects of interest rate hikes in the near term, while easing oil prices on hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough to end the Middle East war kept investors on edge.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil prices ease, gold steady as US-Iran talks in focus
